program_overview.title: Western Canada Grade 12 Math: Pre-calculus 12 and Math 30-1
program_overview.tagline: A second teacher for Grade 12 math in British Columbia and Alberta: functions, logarithms, trigonometry and counting understood properly, in step with your school course.
program_overview.description:
Pre-calculus 12 is one of the Grade 12 courses on British Columbia's mathematics course list, beside Foundations of Mathematics 12 and Calculus 12. In Alberta, Mathematics 30-1 is one of the courses with a provincial diploma exam, and the diploma exam counts for a large share of the final mark. Alberta's diploma exams overview says "The weighting of diploma exams returned to 30% effective September 1, 2023." and "70% of the final mark comes from course work. The remaining 30% comes from the diploma exam." Alberta's provincial achievement tests page adds that "students write diploma exams and provincial achievement tests in a digital environment rather than pencil and paper".

This course runs alongside the student's own Pre-calculus 12 or Math 30-1 class, and we follow the order of the student's school course outline so what is learned here is used in class the same week. What our course teaches: functions and their transformations, including inverses; polynomial, radical and rational functions; exponential and logarithmic functions; trigonometry in radians, with identities and equations; and permutations, combinations and the binomial theorem. Every topic starts from meaning, with graphs and small examples, before the algebra. For Alberta students we add exam technique for the Math 30-1 diploma exam, practised on screen; for BC students we prepare for the school's own unit tests and final exam. Tests and assignments stay the student's own work: we explain, question and review, and the student does the math.

Please read this plainly: Modern Age Coders teaches alongside school and does not grant high school credits in British Columbia, Alberta or any other province. Families who need the credit take the course through their school or an approved provider. What we add is understanding, practice and confidence, in live classes with a real teacher. We make no promise of marks or diploma exam results.

phase_1_functions_and_transformations.title: PHASE 1: Functions, Transformations and Polynomial, Radical and Rational Functions (Months 1-2, Weeks 1-8)
phase_1_functions_and_transformations.description: The function toolkit every Grade 12 topic depends on, then the polynomial, radical and rational families.

week_1_2.title: Weeks 1-2: Starting Point and the Function Toolkit
topics: A starting conversation and short diagnostic: the province, the school, the course outline, the next test and the Grade 11 ideas to refresh
Function notation, domain and range, and reading a graph carefully
Parent functions and their key points
Factoring review: common factors, trinomials and the difference of squares
Solving quadratic equations by factoring and by formula
Setting up a clean notebook system for definitions, examples and mistakes
projects: A one-page function toolkit summary, with a sketch of each parent function and its key points
week_1_2.practice: Short daily sets that mix new work with one or two Grade 11 refresher questions

week_3_4.title: Weeks 3-4: Transformations and Inverses
topics: Translations, stretches and reflections, and the order to apply them
Mapping notation for points on a transformed graph
Writing the equation of a transformed function from its graph
Inverse functions: finding them, graphing them and restricting the domain
Reflections in the line y = x
Common mistakes with horizontal stretches and shifts
projects: A transformation set: ten graphs transformed by hand from mapping rules, then checked with graphing technology
week_3_4.practice: For every transformation, write the mapping rule before sketching
week_3_4.assessment: Month 1 check: a short written test on functions, transformations and inverses, reviewed with written feedback

month_2_polynomial_radical_and_rational_.title: Month 2: Polynomial, Radical and Rational Functions

week_5_6.title: Weeks 5-6: Polynomial Functions
topics: Degree, leading coefficient and end behaviour
Long division and synthetic division
The remainder theorem and the factor theorem
Zeros and their multiplicity, and how the graph behaves at each one
Sketching a polynomial from its factored form
Writing an equation from a graph or from given zeros
projects: A polynomial sketch set with end behaviour, zeros and intercepts explained for each graph
week_5_6.practice: Factor theorem and sketching sets, each answer checked by substitution or graph

week_7_8.title: Weeks 7-8: Radical and Rational Functions
topics: Square root functions and their transformations
Graphing y equal to the square root of a function, and its domain
Rational functions: vertical asymptotes, horizontal asymptotes and holes
Sketching rational functions from their factored form
Solving radical and rational equations graphically and algebraically
Checking for extraneous roots and restricted values
projects: A radical and rational function set with every restriction, asymptote and hole labelled
week_7_8.practice: For every rational function, list restrictions and asymptotes first, then sketch
week_7_8.assessment: Phase 1 assessment: a timed test on functions, transformations and polynomial, radical and rational functions, marked with comments

phase_2_exponents_logarithms_and_trigono.title: PHASE 2: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions, and Trigonometry (Months 3-4, Weeks 9-16)
phase_2_exponents_logarithms_and_trigono.description: Growth, decay and logarithms, then trigonometry in radians with identities and equations.

week_9_10.title: Weeks 9-10: Exponential Functions
topics: Exponential functions and their graphs
Transformations of exponential functions
Solving exponential equations with a common base
Growth and decay: population, half-life and compound interest
Choosing between a linear and an exponential model
Reading an exponential graph to answer a question in context
projects: An applications pack: three real growth or decay situations modelled and solved in full
week_9_10.practice: Mixed exponential equation sets, with answers checked on a graph

week_11_12.title: Weeks 11-12: Logarithms
topics: The logarithm as the inverse of an exponential function
Graphs of logarithmic functions and their transformations
Laws of logarithms and when each one applies
Solving exponential and logarithmic equations, and checking for extraneous roots
Changing the base of a logarithm
Logarithmic scales: sound, earthquakes and pH
projects: A logarithm laws file: ten equations solved in full, with each law named at the step where it is used
week_11_12.practice: One log law proof and three equations every day
week_11_12.assessment: Month 3 check: a written test on exponential and logarithmic functions, reviewed with written feedback

month_4_trigonometry.title: Month 4: Trigonometry in Radians, Identities and Equations

week_13_14.title: Weeks 13-14: Radians, the Unit Circle and Trigonometric Graphs
topics: Radian measure, arc length and converting between radians and degrees
The unit circle and exact values for special angles
Graphs of sine, cosine and tangent
Amplitude, period, phase shift and vertical displacement
Writing a sinusoidal equation from a graph or a situation
Modelling periodic situations such as tides and daylight hours
projects: A sinusoidal model of a real periodic situation, with the equation built from the data and explained
week_13_14.practice: Unit circle and graph sets, each answer checked against a quick sketch

week_15_16.title: Weeks 15-16: Identities and Trigonometric Equations
topics: Reciprocal, quotient and Pythagorean identities
Sum, difference and double angle identities
Proving identities: working one side and writing each step clearly
Solving first and second degree trigonometric equations
Finding all solutions in an interval, and the general solution
Non-permissible values and common mistakes that lose solutions
projects: An identity proof file: ten identities proved in full, with the strategy for each written first
week_15_16.practice: One identity proof and two equations every day, with every solution in the interval listed
week_15_16.assessment: Phase 2 assessment: a mixed review paper on logarithms and trigonometry, marked with written comments

phase_3_counting_and_exam_review.title: PHASE 3: Permutations and Combinations, Combining Functions and Exam Review (Months 5-6, Weeks 17-24)
phase_3_counting_and_exam_review.description: Careful counting, combining functions, then exam review for school finals and, for Alberta students, the Math 30-1 diploma exam.

month_5_counting_and_combining_functions.title: Month 5: Permutations, Combinations and Combining Functions

week_17_18.title: Weeks 17-18: Permutations, Combinations and the Binomial Theorem
topics: The fundamental counting principle
Permutations, including arrangements with repeated items and with restrictions
Combinations, and how to tell a combination problem from a permutation problem
Factorial notation and solving equations with factorials
Pascal's triangle and the binomial theorem
Finding a specific term in a binomial expansion
projects: A counting pack: twelve problems sorted by method, each solved with the reason for the method written first
week_17_18.practice: Mixed counting sets, each starting with the question: does order matter?

week_19_20.title: Weeks 19-20: Combining Functions
topics: Sums, differences, products and quotients of functions, and their graphs
Composition of functions and its domain
Sketching a combined function from the graphs of its parts
Writing a function as a composition of simpler functions
Domain restrictions that come from combining functions
Links back to transformations, logarithms and trigonometry
projects: A combining functions set with graphs, equations and domains explained for each
week_19_20.practice: Short daily sets that combine two functions from earlier units
week_19_20.assessment: Month 5 check: a written test on counting and combining functions, reviewed with written feedback

week_21_22.title: Weeks 21-22: Mixed Review and Written Solutions
topics: Making a one-page summary for each unit of the school course
Mixed review sets that move between units without warning
Full written solutions that show every step
Using graphing technology to check, not to replace, the algebra
Building and using a personal mistakes list
Reading the teacher's exam outline so revision matches what will be assessed
projects: A personal review pack: unit summaries and a mistakes list with a corrected example for each mistake
week_21_22.practice: A mixed review set after every class, with every mistake written up and fixed

week_23_24.title: Weeks 23-24: Timed Practice for School Finals and the Alberta Diploma Exam
topics: Timed review papers in the style of school final exams, with careful review afterwards
For Alberta students: pacing a long exam and checking answers before moving on
For Alberta students: practising on screen, since diploma exams are written in a digital environment
Reading Alberta's current diploma exam schedule and instructions together
For BC students: matching revision to the school's own final exam outline
A calm exam-week routine: sleep, short practice and one last review of the mistakes list
projects: Two reviewed timed papers and a written exam-week plan
week_23_24.practice: A timed mixed review each week, reviewed in class
week_23_24.assessment: Final assessment: a timed review paper plus a short live walk-through of two of the student's own solutions

faqs.question: Does this course give my child a high school credit in BC or Alberta?
faqs.answer: No. Modern Age Coders teaches alongside school and does not grant high school credits in British Columbia, Alberta or any other province. A family who needs the Pre-calculus 12 or Math 30-1 credit takes the course through the student's school or an approved provider. Our course helps the student understand and do well in the school course they are already taking.

faqs.question: Which courses is this for?
faqs.answer: Pre-calculus 12 in British Columbia, which is on BC's mathematics course list, and Mathematics 30-1 in Alberta, which is on Alberta's list of diploma exam courses. Both are Grade 12 courses heavy in functions, so we teach them together while following each student's own school course outline.

faqs.question: What topics does the course teach?
faqs.answer: Functions and transformations, including inverses; polynomial, radical and rational functions; exponential and logarithmic functions; trigonometry in radians, with identities and equations; and permutations, combinations and the binomial theorem, plus combining functions. Your school's course outline gives the exact list and order for your class, and we follow it.

faqs.question: How much is the Math 30-1 diploma exam worth?
faqs.answer: Alberta's diploma exams overview says "The weighting of diploma exams returned to 30% effective September 1, 2023." and "70% of the final mark comes from course work. The remaining 30% comes from the diploma exam." Mathematics 30-1 is one of the diploma exam courses on that page.

faqs.question: Do you prepare Alberta students for the Math 30-1 diploma exam?
faqs.answer: Yes, alongside their school course. We teach the mathematics, then exam technique: pacing, checking and timed practice papers with careful review. Alberta says "students write diploma exams and provincial achievement tests in a digital environment rather than pencil and paper", so some practice is done on screen. Exam schedules can change, so we read Alberta's current diploma exam information with each student. We make no promise of marks or results.

faqs.question: What comes after Pre-calculus 12?
faqs.answer: BC's mathematics course list also includes Calculus 12, and many university programs in science, engineering and computer science build on pre-calculus. The functions, logarithms and trigonometry in this course are exactly what calculus uses. Always check each university's current admission page for its own requirements.

faqs.question: Does the course follow my school's order?
faqs.answer: Yes. Schools order the units differently, so we use the student's own course outline and next test date to set the pace. The plan on this page shows our standard sequence, and each batch follows the order of its students' schools as closely as possible.

faqs.question: Will you do my child's assignments or tests?
faqs.answer: No. School work stays the student's own. We explain concepts, ask questions, review work the student has written and suggest how to improve it, and we follow the school's rules on outside help. That is also the only kind of help that lasts into the exam room.

faqs.question: Can my child join partway through the school year?
faqs.answer: Yes, the course is joinable any month. We start from the student's current unit and next test, fill gaps from earlier units as needed, and keep pace with the school course from then on.

faqs.question: How are the classes run?
faqs.answer: Live online classes, twice a week, with a real teacher, in a group of 15 to 20 students, a mini batch of up to 6, or 1-on-1. Weekdays or weekends, flexible: choose your batch, or for a very personalised plan choose 1-on-1 at your convenience, weekend mornings or weekdays. Current fees for your region are shown in the pricing section of this page.

faqs.question: Can we try a class first?
faqs.answer: Yes. Book a free demo class. The teacher looks at where your child is in Pre-calculus 12 or Math 30-1, works through a short problem with them, and suggests whether group, mini batch or 1-on-1 classes fit best. There is no obligation to enrol.
